The department is a unique function within Policing and across the Eastern Region, providing specialist intelligence support to ROCU and Force led operations as well as supporting partner agencies in their fight against serious and organised crime. The SIU is dedicated to supporting operations tackling the highest harm and threat areas, across multiple crime types, exploiting and enhancing intelligence from multiple sensitive data sources in order to provide key stakeholders with the best opportunities to conduct enforcement, recover assets, seize criminal commodity and bring offenders to justice. We provide intelligence support to Crime In Action investigations (kidnap and extortion) as well as supporting the prevention, mitigation and management of Threats to Life (TTL) in order to safeguard vulnerable people. Managing intelligence against tasked operations across the Eastern Region, you will gain first-hand knowledge of Serious and Organised Crime detection and disruption techniques and conduct intelligence collection against Organised Crime Groups (OCG’s) involved in firearms and drugs importation/supply, organised immigration crime/human trafficking, modern day slavery, child sexual exploitation, cyber enabled criminality and financial crime across the region. The work conducted by the SIU delivers significant operational results day in day out. The SIU can often be an exhilarating and fast-moving working environment where innovation, problem solving and the use of the latest technology and intelligence techniques are utilised to keep up with the ever-growing complexity and sophistication of serious organised crime. You can expect a varied and fulfilling career within this business area, with no two days ever being quite the same. Your work will be fundamental in contributing to the impressive results that make the headlines and your role will be integral in the disruption of organised crime in the Eastern Region. The role involves undertaking an 8-week rotational shift pattern as the SIU operates between the hours of 8am and 6pm. You will work a mix of 8am-4pm/8am-4.30pm/9.30-6pm shifts including an on- call weekend (Fri-Sun) and a weekday on-call (Mon-Thurs). Tackling serious and organised criminals requires applicants to be able to be flexible to meet operational demands (sometimes at short notice). Diligence and a strong team work ethic are key. Innovative ways of thinking and problem solving are desirable. We are recruiting for an experienced intelligence officer who can demonstrate an aptitude for intelligence research and an investigative mindset combined with the ability to learn. Experience within a covert environment is desirable but not essential. A full training pathway and mentoring will be provided to the successful candidates, and they will be expected to attain IPP accreditation if not already held. The departments are unique, in that they offer opportunities to work and develop individuals professionally in specialist areas, often delivering capabilities that are provided by local forces. We are committed to building a leadership team that reflects the diversity of the communities we serve. We actively encourage applications from individuals who are currently underrepresented at senior levels, including women, Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic candidates, disabled people, and those from LGBTQ+ communities. Our clients and counterparties span African businesses, investors, financial institutions, exchanges, development institutions and international capital looking at the continent. We are now looking for an exceptional Associate, Valuation & Financial Modelling to join the team. This is not a back office modelling role. You will work directly with the founding team on live mandates, investment decisions and transaction questions where the numbers determine what happens next. You may be analysing whether a company is ready for institutional capital. You may be modelling what an acquisition should be worth. You may be testing the economics of a public markets transaction. You may be examining dilution, leverage, returns or exit outcomes. You may be helping an investor decide whether an African opportunity deserves another dollar of diligence. And you will be expected to have a view. Why this role is unusual 0to1 is intentionally building a small, senior led team. That means associates work close to the decision makers. You will work alongside a founding team with experience spanning advisory, enterprise strategy, development finance, public sector transformation, capital markets and work with institutions including the World Bank and USAID. You will also have access to an independent bench of senior advisers that includes former executives and leaders from major listed companies in Africa and the United States. For the right person, that creates something difficult to replicate in a conventional analyst programme: direct apprenticeship to people who have actually led companies, advised institutions, allocated capital and sat on the other side of the boardroom table. You will not spend three years waiting to be allowed into the room. You will be in the room. The work You will build and interrogate the financial analysis behind our mandates, including: • three statement financial models • DCF and comparable company valuation • precedent transaction analysis • acquisition and investment models • private equity and shareholder return analysis • scenario and sensitivity modelling • capital structure analysis • debt capacity and financing scenarios • cap tables and dilution analysis • transaction economics • valuation ranges and negotiation support • IPO and capital markets readiness analysis • management forecast review • financial performance and cash conversion analysis But we are not hiring someone simply to build spreadsheets. We are hiring someone who can look at a model and ask: What assumption is doing too much work here? Why is EBITDA growing but cash disappearing? What happens to returns if the exit multiple compresses? Is management's forecast credible? What price can the investor pay and still achieve the required return? What would make this company more valuable twelve months from now? That is where modelling becomes advisory. What you will be exposed to Our work is increasingly Africa wide. You may find yourself working across East, West, Southern and Central Africa, analysing companies in markets that global investors are only beginning to understand properly. You will gain exposure to: private equity M&A capital raising public markets IPO readiness cross border transactions market entry enterprise value creation portfolio company strategy sovereign and development finance new forms of capital and transaction structures emerging across African markets We are also working on areas that do not always fit neatly into traditional advisory boxes, including how AI changes enterprise value, how African companies prepare for institutional ownership, how regional exchanges can create new capital corridors and how growth businesses move from founder led companies into investable institutions. We are offering the opportunity to help build one.
